PullRequest.Title: sessions: stop chat header spinner once its own chat completes
PullRequest.Body:

Fixes #339337

When chats are shown side by side in the Agents window, a chat that had already finished (for example a side chat or subagent) kept the animated pixel spinner in its header for as long as another chat in the same session was still running.

## What changed

`SessionHeaderBar` (shared by the per-group `ChatHeader` and the single-group `SessionHeader`) fed its status icon the session's `status`, which aggregates all chats and stays in progress while any of them is running. It now uses the status of the chat the header is showing, and falls back to the session's status only when there is no chat.

This matches how the header already derives the read state (#340331), the untitled title, and title editability from the active chat. It also matches the chat's own row in the sessions list.

## Notes for reviewers

- The single-group session header changes too, because its title follows the active chat: while viewing a finished chat, the header no longer spins because a different chat in the session is running. The session's row in the sessions list still shows the aggregate status.
- Agent host chat statuses already present an active chat on a known-unreachable remote host as an error, so the header now shows that error state instead of a spinner, matching the chat's row in the sessions list.
- Copilot chat sessions have a single chat whose status is the session's status, so their behavior is unchanged.

## How to test

1. In the Agents window, open a session with two chats shown side by side (for example a side chat next to the main chat).
2. Send a prompt to both, then let one finish while the other keeps running.
3. The finished chat's header should show its completed/unread icon instead of the pixel spinner, while the running chat's header keeps the spinner.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`: passed
- `npm run build-fast -- --client-only`: passed
- `./scripts/test.sh --reporter dot --run src/vs/sessions/test/browser/sessionHeader.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/test/browser/sessionStatusIcon.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/test/browser/chatGroupsView.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/test/browser/sessionView.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/test/browser/sessionsPart.test.ts`: 165 passing. The new regression test fails without the fix.
- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/sessions/browser/parts/sessionHeaderBar.ts src/vs/sessions/test/browser/sessionHeader.test.ts`: no problems
- Not manually verified in a running Code OSS build.

Scenarios.Scenario: Two chats shown side by side while one chat completes and the peer remains in progress
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A provider-fed chat status observable invalidates that chat header's existing synchronous autorun; the autorun updates the cached status icon before the next paint. No subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network operation is reached by the changed header code.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: The number of mounted visible chat headers and status transitions. Each changed chat status affects its own header; before the diff, aggregate session status could also invalidate peer headers, while activeChat.status was already observed in each header for title/editability.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One synchronous autorun per mounted header. StatusIcon coalesces identical glyphs through _currentCacheKey; a real status/glyph transition schedules at most two animation-frame callbacks and one 220 ms cleanup timer for that header. There is no async fan-out or shared queue.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold header creation builds one icon. Warm updates with the same glyph recolor the active element without rebuilding it; status changes swap one icon and dispose the outgoing one. The diff does not alter cache keys or lifecycle.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed line replaces session.status.read with activeChat.status.read, and the same autorun already reads activeChat.status later in _updateHeader. SessionStatusIcon source confirms cached DOM behavior and no external boundary.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact numbers of simultaneous visible chat groups and status transitions vary, but work is bounded per mounted header and the dependency change reduces rather than increases peer invalidations.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The intended extra icon transition occurs only when that header's displayed chat status changes, and peer-chat aggregate invalidations are removed.

Scenarios.Scenario: Single-group session header follows the active chat while another chat in the session continues running
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Changing the active chat or its status synchronously reruns SessionHeaderBar._updateHeader and updates title, classes, ARIA text, and the cached icon on the UI thread. The changed line introduces no external boundary and does not add a new autorun dependency because activeChat.status was already read for title selection.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Active-chat switches and status transitions within one open session, independent of total session history except existing title ancestor lookup. The diff does not change ancestor traversal or collection cardinality.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A single synchronous autorun for the mounted session header; active-chat changes are serialized by the observable transaction mechanism, with no concurrent I/O or worker activity introduced here.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: SessionHeaderBar resets the icon cache only when context identity changes. Within one context, same-glyph updates reuse the active DOM node and status transitions retain outgoing DOM only for the existing bounded cross-fade timeout.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: SessionHeader passes session.activeChat into the bar, and the inspected call path reaches only synchronous observable reads and cached DOM rendering.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Sessions may contain varying numbers of chats, but the changed status selection is O(1) and does not traverse that collection.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression; the change alters which already-observed scalar status is rendered without adding repeated work, retention, or boundary calls.

Scenarios.Scenario: Header context temporarily has no chat
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The header falls back to reading session.status and renders through the same synchronous cached icon path. This fallback behavior is unchanged by the diff.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One header update per session status transition; no collection scaling is introduced.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One synchronous autorun, no asynchronous work or external boundary.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing icon cache and bounded cross-fade behavior are unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the conditional's false branch is the exact pre-diff session.status.read call.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: This state may be uncommon for active sessions, but the performance behavior is directly unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression because the no-chat execution path preserves prior work and frequency.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete two-file diff and traced the changed production autorun through SessionHeader, ChatHeader, and SessionStatusIcon. The active-chat status read adds no new invalidation source, icon updates are cached and lifecycle-bounded, peer aggregate invalidations are reduced, and no expensive process/IPC/filesystem/database/network boundary is introduced. Test-only observable changes and DOM assertions do not affect product runtime.
